stories.headline: Humanoid robot maker Agility to go public via Michael Klein SPAC at ~$2.5B

key_facts.fact: Agility Robotics will go public by merging with Michael Klein's SPAC, Churchill Capital Corp XI, in a deal valuing the company at about $2.5 billion, listing under the ticker AGLT
key_facts.excerpt: Agility is set to merge with Michael Klein's special purpose acquisition company (SPAC), Churchill Capital Corp. XI, and to be listed on the stock exchange under the ticker symbol AGLT.

key_facts.fact: The transaction is expected to generate over $600 million in gross proceeds: $420 million in cash from Churchill XI plus more than $200 million via a PIPE led by Foxconn, an existing Agility backer
key_facts.excerpt: The companies expect to generate gross proceeds of over $600 million from the transaction, including $420 million in cash from Churchill XI and over $200 million through a private investment in common stock (PIPE), led by Foxconn.

key_facts.fact: Agility's flagship bipedal humanoid robot, Digit, is used by Amazon, logistics firm QXO, auto-parts maker Schaeffler, and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada to automate moving and stacking heavy containers
key_facts.excerpt: Agility's clients include Amazon.com, which uses the company's products in its warehouses, the logistics firm QXO, the automotive components manufacturer Schaeffler, and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada... Agility's flagship humanoid robot is known as Digit.

key_facts.fact: Other investors in Agility include Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank
key_facts.excerpt: Other investors in Agility include Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank.

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported the deal on June 24 based on comments by Agility executives; Digit is used at manufacturing facilities and warehouses by companies such as Amazon
key_facts.excerpt: Agility, Maker of Humanlike Robots, to Go Public in $2.5 Billion SPAC Deal. Agility's humanoid robot, Digit, is used at manufacturing facilities and warehouses by companies such as Amazon. This story appeared on wsj.com, 2026-06-24.

stories.headline: EUV laser startup xLight in talks to raise $350M led by Bain Capital, Boardman Bay

key_facts.fact: xLight, a startup developing advanced free-electron lasers for EUV chipmaking machines, told investors it is in talks to raise $350 million, led by Boardman Bay and Bain Capital
key_facts.excerpt: xLight, a startup developing advanced lasers for EUV machines, told investors that it is in talks to raise $350M led by Boardman Bay and Bain Capital (The Information)

key_facts.fact: The US-backed chipmaking startup is chaired by a former Intel CEO; Pat Gelsinger, ousted as Intel's CEO, backs xLight as a general partner at Playground Global
key_facts.excerpt: U.S.-Backed Chipmaking Startup Chaired by Former Intel CEO Is Raising $350 Million

key_facts.fact: xLight is building utility-scale free-electron lasers powered by particle accelerators to produce EUV light for next-generation chipmaking, aiming to challenge ASML's lithography dominance
key_facts.excerpt: Now a general partner at Playground Global, he's backing 10 deep-tech startups - but one clearly stands out: xLight, a semiconductor company aiming to revive Moore's Law using free electron lasers.

key_facts.fact: The new round follows a $40 million Series B closed in July 2025, led by Playground Global with participation from Boardman Bay Capital Management
key_facts.excerpt: xLight... today announced it has closed an oversubscribed $40M Series B equity raise. The round was led by Playground Global... and joined by Boardman Bay Capital Management.

key_facts.fact: In December 2025 xLight signed a letter of intent with the US Commerce Department for $150 million in proposed CHIPS Act incentives, which would give the agency $150 million of equity in the startup
key_facts.excerpt: Silicon Valley startup XLight announced on Monday that it has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for $150 million in proposed federal incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act... the Commerce Department would receive $150 million of equity in XLight.

stories.headline: Qualcomm in talks to design custom chips for ByteDance using Alphawave tech

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm is in talks to provide custom chip-design services to China's ByteDance, parent of TikTok, according to four people familiar with the matter
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm is in talks to provide chip-design services to China's ByteDance, four people familiar with the matter said, as the U.S. company seeks to reduce dependence on the smartphone market, its biggest revenue source.

key_facts.fact: The chips would be based in part on technology owned by Alphawave Semi, a high-speed connectivity specialist Qualcomm acquired in 2025
key_facts.excerpt: The chips would be based in part on technology owned by AlphaWave Semi, a high-speed connectivity specialist Qualcomm acquired last year, two of the sources said.

key_facts.fact: The discussion involves designing video processing units (VPUs), with an eye toward starting mass production by the end of the year; ByteDance is separately developing an AI inference chip and custom CPUs
key_facts.excerpt: One of the sources said the discussion involves the designing of video processing units (VPUs), with an eye toward starting mass production by the end of the year. Reuters reported earlier that ByteDance is developing an AI chip for inference tasks and custom central processing units (CPUs).

key_facts.fact: A successful deal would make ByteDance an early customer of Qualcomm's chip-design services operation; the outcome remains uncertain and ByteDance could pursue other partners
key_facts.excerpt: If successful, the negotiations would make ByteDance... an early customer of Qualcomm's chip-design services operation... While the discussions are underway, the outcome remains uncertain... ByteDance could pursue different partners.

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm is working to break into the data center chip market, developing three kinds of chips: CPUs, inference accelerators, and custom ASICs, competing with Broadcom and Marvell
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm is working to break into the booming data center chip market and working with customers on three kinds of chips: CPUs, accelerators for inference, and custom chips called ASICs, a fast-growing market for rivals such as Broadcom and Marvell.

stories.headline: Nvidia AI chip prices double on China's black market amid US export crackdown

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's flagship DGX B300 server, which contains eight Blackwell GPUs, now sells for more than 8 million yuan ($1.1 million) on China's black market, roughly double its price six months ago (up from 4 million yuan), per FT interviews with Chinese chip traders
key_facts.excerpt: The sharpest increase has been seen in Nvidia's DGX B300 server, one of the company's flagship AI systems powered by eight Blackwell graphics processors. Chinese traders told the newspaper that the server now sells for more than 8 million yuan ($1.1 million), roughly double its price from six months ago and well above its US retail value.

key_facts.fact: The RTX 6000 Pro chip, widely used by startups developing large language models, has risen from around 50,000 yuan to as much as 130,000 yuan
key_facts.excerpt: The RTX 6000 Pro chip, widely used by start-ups developing large language models, is also reported to have risen from around 50,000 yuan to a maximum of 130,000 yuan.

key_facts.fact: Prices surged after US authorities stepped up investigations into chip-smuggling operations late last year, with regulators in Taiwan and Malaysia also cracking down on re-export routes used to move hardware into China
key_facts.excerpt: Supplies became particularly constrained after US authorities stepped up investigations into suspected chip-smuggling operations late last year. The pressure has increased further as regulators in Taiwan and Malaysia crack down on re-export routes that were frequently used to move restricted hardware into China.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia described building data centers using illegally imported products as 'a dead end,' emphasizing it does not provide support or repairs for restricted hardware
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia, for its part, has described the construction of data centres using illegally imported products as 'a dead end', emphasising that it does not provide support or repairs for restricted hardware.

stories.headline: SK Hynix to raise up to $29.4B via Nasdaq ADR listing, trading to start July 10

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said on June 24 it plans to raise up to 45.45 trillion won ($29.4 billion) via a stock offering to list American depositary receipts (ADRs) on Nasdaq, to fund production facility purchases
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix Inc. said Wednesday it plans to raise up to 45.45 trillion won (US$29.4 billion) via stock offering for the listing of its American depositary receipts (ADRs) on the Nasdaq market in order to fund its production facility purchases.

key_facts.fact: New shares will be sold at 2.55 million won and listed in Seoul on July 29; ADRs priced at 255,500 won apiece will list on Nasdaq on July 10
key_facts.excerpt: The new shares will be sold at 2.55 million won and listed on July 29, and ADRs will be priced at 255,500 won apiece, and listed on the Nasdaq on July 10, SK hynix said in a regulatory filing.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix, the main supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to Nvidia, overtook Samsung Electronics this week to become South Korea's most valuable company by common stock
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix, which overtook Samsung Electronics as Korea's most valuable company by common stock this week, is preparing a U.S. stock listing that could raise up to $20 billion to bankroll its AI memory chip expansion.

key_facts.fact: The ADR listing is part of SK Hynix's broader effort to deepen integration into the US AI ecosystem; Citigroup, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Bank of America are the arrangers
key_facts.excerpt: The planned ADR listing is also seen as part of SK hynix's broader effort to deepen its integration into the U.S. AI ecosystem.

stories.headline: Cerebras Q1 revenue jumps 94% to $193M, but shares fall on margin guidance

key_facts.fact: In its first quarterly report since its May IPO, Cerebras posted Q1 FY2026 GAAP revenue of $193.4 million, up 94% year-over-year (from $99.5 million) and 13% sequentially
key_facts.excerpt: The company reported revenue of $193.4 million for the first quarter, compared with $99.5 million in the same period a year ago.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras reported a GAAP net loss of $14.0 million; its adjusted (core) net loss of $2.5 million was far narrower than analysts' expected loss of $36.75 million
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras said its adjusted net loss for the quarter was $2.5 million, narrower than analyst estimates of an adjusted loss of $36.75 million.

key_facts.fact: The company guided full-year 2026 adjusted gross margins to 38-41%, down from 47% core (45% GAAP) in Q1 and far below rivals such as Nvidia (mid-70s%) and AMD (mid-50s%); shares fell about 10% in extended trading
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras forecast adjusted gross margins of 38% to 41% for full-year 2026, down from the 47% it reported for the first quarter... sending shares down 10% in extended trading on Tuesday... far below those of rivals such as Nvidia, whose gross margins are in the mid-70% area, and Advanced Micro Devices, whose gross margins are in the mid-50% range.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras cited a multi-year OpenAI deal exceeding $20 billion for 750MW of compute and an AWS fast-inference partnership; it guided 2026 core revenue to $855-865 million, up about 69% at the midpoint
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras announced a multi-year OpenAI deal exceeding $20 billion for 750MW of compute, a multi-year AWS partnership for fast inference... 2026 core revenue guidance is $855-865 million, up 69% year-over-year at the midpoint.

stories.headline: Hadrian reportedly in talks to raise $1B at $7.5B valuation; company calls it inaccurate

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on June 23 that Hadrian Automation, which builds AI-powered factories to produce space and defense parts, is in talks to raise as much as $1 billion at a valuation of about $7.5 billion (including money raised)
key_facts.excerpt: Defense manufacturing startup Hadrian Automation Inc. has discussed a new funding round that would more than quadruple its valuation to about $7.5 billion, including money raised... The company has been in talks with investors to raise as much as $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: A Hadrian spokesperson called the reported figures 'inaccurate' and declined to elaborate; the financing details are not final and could still change
key_facts.excerpt: Hadrian Automation... has denied a report that it is discussing a new funding round that would see it raise $1 billion at a valuation of $7.5 billion... a Hadrian spokesperson said the information is 'inaccurate' and declined to say more.

key_facts.fact: The reported $7.5 billion valuation would more than quadruple the $1.6 billion valuation Hadrian reached after a January 2026 round led by T. Rowe Price
key_facts.excerpt: The reported valuation would more than quadruple the $1.6 billion valuation the company achieved after receiving funding in January, according to the report.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2020, Hadrian operates four US factories, including one in Cherokee, Alabama that opened in March and manufactures submarine parts for the US Navy
key_facts.excerpt: The company operates four factories in the United States, including one in Cherokee, Alabama, that opened in March and manufactures submarine parts for the U.S. Navy.

key_facts.fact: Hadrian raised $260 million in a Series C round in July 2025 led by Founders Fund and Lux Capital
key_facts.excerpt: Hadrian currently operates four factories, with its most recent facility opening in Cherokee, Alabama to support a $2.4 billion contract with the US Navy for submarine components.
